title: How to Clean and Optimize an SVG File
description: Learn what SVG optimization removes, why sanitized preview matters, and how to inspect an SVG before using it on a website.
intro: SVG is a text-based vector format that can include more than shapes: markup may contain metadata, references or active content. Optimization can reduce unnecessary bytes, while sanitization helps limit risky content before preview or reuse.

sections.heading: Why SVG files can be unexpectedly large
paragraphs: Design software may include editor metadata, comments, unused definitions, redundant whitespace and repeated attributes. These can increase file size without changing the visible illustration.
SVG is XML-based, so hand-editing can introduce malformed markup. Keep a source copy before optimizing, especially when the file is part of a build pipeline.

sections.heading: Treat SVG markup as untrusted input
paragraphs: SVG content can include scripts, external resource references and other markup that should not be casually executed. Do not open untrusted SVG source as an unrestricted active document.
A sanitized preview should restrict scripts and external references. Previewing safely is distinct from proving that an SVG is harmless in every application or embedding context.

sections.heading: Optimize and compare
paragraphs: Use SVG Optimizer & Cleaner to remove whitespace and unsafe SVG content locally. Compare the output with the original in a trusted viewer, check that the artwork remains correct, and measure the resulting file size.
For raster images, use the Image Format Converter or Image Compressor; raster compression and SVG cleanup are different operations.

faq.question: Will SVG optimization change how an illustration looks?
faq.answer: It should preserve intended visuals, but unusual markup or unsupported features may behave differently. Compare the result before publishing.

faq.question: Can SVG contain scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. SVG is markup and may contain active or externally referenced content. Treat untrusted SVG files carefully and use sanitized previews.

faq.question: Does a smaller SVG always render faster?
faq.answer: Smaller files can reduce transfer size, but rendering cost also depends on path complexity, document structure and how the page uses the image.

faq.question: Should I overwrite my original SVG?
faq.answer: Keep the source file until you have reviewed the optimized output and confirmed it works in the target environment.
